title: New Zealand Dollar Advances as Ruling Party Gets Election Edge

title: Treasury Rally Gets New Boost as Election Hammers the AI Trade
summary: Wall Street sees the Treasury market emerging as a winner from the Democratic landslide in the US midterm elections, giving traders another reason to rethink this year’s sharp selloff.

title: Watching Wall Street, Deadly Mass Shooting in Poland, Back to Work After Blue Wave
summary: The news doesn’t stop when markets close. Hosts David Gura, Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo bring clarity, context and a bit of humor to the weekend’s biggest headlines, LIVE from New York. Joined by Fmr. Deputy Secretary of State & Fmr. US Special Representative for North Korea Stephen Biegun, SMBC Nikko Securities Chief Economist Joe Lavorgna, Author & Journalist Hannah Howard, North Carolina Rep Elect Paul Barringer, Virginia Rep Elect Shannon Taylor, Rising Communications President Leslie Shedd and Causeway Strategy Group Principal John McCarthy. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Bookmarked: News Stories On Our Reading List
summary: The Met Gala announces a 'normie' theme, the end of floppy disks, lawsuit over McRib contents, and the Hall of Fame of Toys: Join hosts David Gura, Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo on Bloomberg This Weekend for Bookmarked, where they share stories that caught their attention over the past week. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: By The Way: Headlines You May Have Missed
summary: Choosing who to give Christmas presents to, a Christmas themed cruise, students making a deposit for college and then not attending, and the SATs and AP tests tackle AI cheating: Join Lisa Mateo, David Gura and Christina Ruffini for a roundup of headlines you may have missed, but gotta see. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Markets Brace for Washington Policy Battles
summary: On Bloomberg This Weekend, SMBC Nikko Securities Chief Economist Joe Lavorgna says affordability helped drive the midterm results but argues the underlying US economy remains healthy and major policy changes may be limited by divided government. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Lavorgna discusses the outlook for AI investment, inflation and markets as Washington prepares for two years of potential policy.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Israel’s Election Fight Shifts to Coalition Building
summary: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg Middle East reporter Dan Williams explains why Gadi Eisenkot has been given the first opportunity to form Israel’s next government despite Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc winning more seats. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Williams discusses the role of Arab parties in coalition negotiations, Netanyahu’s political future and what could happen if Eisenkot fails to assemble a majority. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Can Europe Afford Its Welfare State?
summary: Europe’s postwar welfare state was built for a younger, growing population. Today, aging communities are putting pensions, health care and public finances under mounting strain. As governments try to fund defense, infrastructure and education at the same time, the fight over who pays is spilling into politics and the streets. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: New House Democrats Set Their Priorities
summary: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Democratic Reps.-elect Paul Barringer of North Carolina and Shannon Taylor of Virginia say voters sent them to Washington with a mandate to address affordability, health care and government accountability. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, they discuss working across the aisle, restoring congressional authority and responding to concerns about tariffs, data centers and the cost of living.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Luxury Gyms Turn Fitness Into a Family Affair
summary: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg Pursuits writer Hannah Howard explains how high end fitness clubs are courting families with everything from child care and swimming lessons to homework help and activities for older kids. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Howard discusses why parents are willing to pay hundreds or even more than $1,000 a month for clubs that combine workouts, activities and family time under one roof. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Seattle and Las Vegas Make Their NBA Pitch
summary: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg senior sports reporter Randall Williams explains why the NBA’s potential expansion to Seattle and Las Vegas could generate billions of dollars while raising questions about the financial returns for existing owners. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Williams also examines the competition among prospective ownership groups, LIV Golf’s struggles and the labor battle threatening Major League Baseball’s next season. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Ukraine Peace Push Returns to Abu Dhabi
summary: US, Ukrainian and Russian delegations are scheduled to meet in Abu Dhabi on November 10th and 11th, with Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner expected to represent the US. Joining Bloomberg This Weekend former Deputy Secretary of State Stephen Biegun discusses how a Democratic-controlled Congress could bring greater scrutiny to President Donald Trump’s foreign policy as the US renews efforts to negotiate an end to Russia’s war in Ukraine. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Wall Street Races for Megadeals as Countdown Begins on Trump Era
summary: President Donald Trump’s return to the White House changed the political calculus around mergers and acquisitions, reviving companies’ desire for dream deals that had become difficult to pull off. Now, corporate America is on the clock.

title: Democratic Sweep Tests Trump-Linked Trades Across Latin America
summary: Investors who spent the past year factoring countries’ standing with Donald Trump into their Latin America trades are confronting a new variable: a Democratic-controlled US Congress.

title: How Everyday Apps Feed Police Surveillance
summary: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg investigative journalist Ryan Gallagher explains how location data collected through everyday smartphone apps can ultimately be sold to law enforcement agencies, often without users knowing where their information ends up. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Gallagher details how Penlink’s surveillance technology can track phones using commercially obtained data and why its use has fueled calls for greater privacy protections and oversight. (Source: Bloomberg)
